15.translation: He states that these alone are the causes of all action, with the verse beginning ‘śarīra.’ Action being undertaken by the five already stated is subsumed within just three; thus it is said ‘by body, speech, and mind,’ because action is well known as threefold—bodily, verbal, and mental. Whatever action, righteous or unrighteous, a man performs by the body and the others, these five are the causes of all that action.
word_for_word: being the causes of all action
because it is well known thus
by the body and the others

16.translation: Then what follows? On this he says, with the verse beginning ‘tatra.’ Since in every action these five are the causes, this being so, one who nevertheless sees the Self—which is absolute, without limiting adjuncts, and unattached—as the agent, because his understanding is unrefined through abandoning the teaching of scripture and teacher, is of wrong understanding; that person does not see correctly.
word_for_word: as the agent; as the doer
through abandoning the teaching of scripture and teacher
because his understanding is unrefined; untrained
